methods.label: Classify the attachment sides
methods.explanation:
Rotating the regular pentagon carries each allowed triangle position to another, so we should compare the spacing of the two chosen sides rather than their labels.

Any two sides are either adjacent or nonadjacent. Every adjacent pair is a rotated copy of the pair \(AB,BC\). For a nonadjacent pair, exactly one side lies between the chosen sides along the shorter route around the pentagon. Thus every nonadjacent pair is a rotated copy of \(AB,CD\). These two cases include every possible selection and give at most two different figures.

To check that the two cases are not congruent, consider their corners. Each pentagon angle is
\[
\frac{(5-2)180^\circ}{5}=108^\circ,
\]
and each equilateral triangle angle is \(60^\circ\). When the attachment sides are adjacent, their common vertex becomes an inward corner with interior angle \(108^\circ+60^\circ+60^\circ=228^\circ\). With nonadjacent attachments, no vertex receives two triangles; its boundary angles are only \(60^\circ\), \(108^\circ\), or \(168^\circ\), so there is no inward corner. Congruent figures must have matching corners, so these cases are distinct.

Therefore there are \(\boxed{2}\) non-congruent figures, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
